title.narrative: Integrated multi-sector support for conflict-affected IDPs in Kuyu woreda, N/Shewa Zone, Oromia Region.

description.narrative: ltpgtThis project proposal is formulated based on the first reserve allocation of UNOCHA, 2024, with the project code CBPF-ETH-24-R-NGO-33277. The project's goal is to meet the humanitarian needs of conflict-affected IDPs through multi-sectoral response that encompasses ES/NFI, WASH, Nutrition, and MPC in Kuyu Woreda of North Shewa Zone, Oromia region.ltbrgtBased on the MIRA Report 2023, the North Shewa Zone, particularly Kuyu Woreda, is experiencing significant humanitarian needs in various sectors including Food/Nutrition, Shelter, NFIs and WASH. Notably, shelter damage is a critical issue in the zone, with reports from Busa Gonofa indicating that approximately 4,867 houses have been burnt, damaged, or looted in eight conflict-affected woredas. Moreover, over 10,700 individuals from 23 villages have been displaced and have sought refuge in neighboring towns like Fiche, Gebreguracha, and Birirti. Though, majority of the displaced persons are staying with host communities, the living conditions are inadequate and overcrowded, with an average rent of 1,000-1,500 birrs for a 12 square meter room. Due to financial constraints, some IDPs are at risk of eviction, while others are forced to live outside on verandas.ltbrgtRegarding Nutrition, the physical condition of females has deteriorated or become emaciated due to food shortages following displacement. The management of acute malnutrition in all four woredas has been disrupted due to damage to health facilities, leading to an increase in Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) and Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM) among children under five and Pregnant and Lactating Women (PLWs) in the zone. For instance, SAM cases have surged from 2,950 in the 1st quarter of 2023 to 6,984 in the 4th quarter of 2023, with a proxy Global Acute Malnutrition (GAM) rate of 4.4% for the zone.ltbrgtThe water supply system in Kuyu Woreda has been severely disrupted due to the conflict, resulting in 15% of water supply schemes being non-functional. This has led to acute water shortages and increased risks of waterborne diseases for many residents. The cost of water from a protected source in Kuyu Town is 20 birr per 25-liter jerrican. Schools and health institutions in Kuyu currently lack WASH services, meaning they do not have access to water and latrines.ltbrgtANE has developed an integrated multi-sectoral proposal to address the urgent needs of various sectors in Kuyu Woreda, including ES/NFI, WASH, Nutrition, and MPC. The proposal involves implementing community-based interventions in each sector. The expected outcomes of these interventions include enhanced access to Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) services for IDPs, returnees, and host community members, training of community nutrition workers in vulnerable communities, improved access to safe water sources, and improved access to safe sanitation services.ltbrgtANE will prioritize the involvement of local communities and organizations at every stage. By collaborating with local Organizations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs) and community groups, the project aims to make interventions culturally relevant, context-specific, and sustainable. The project will also utilize local knowledge and resources to promote community ownership and resilience. This strategy not only improves immediate humanitarian responses but also reinforces the long-term capabilities of local institutions and communities, promoting self-reliance and empowerment. Throughout the project management cycle and in all humanitarian sectors, ANE ensures the safety and dignity of target communities, particularly the population at risk of protection, by providing access to quality and equitable services, being accountable for its interventions, and focusing on the participation and empowerment of the target communities. To address the needs of all sectors, an estimated budget of 600,000 USD is required. The project is expected to take 8 months, implementing from 15-Aug-2024 to 14-Apr-2025.lt/pgt
